shifts.summary: The shift was overall Easy to Moderate. Reasoning was generally Moderate but some candidates found it Easy or Moderate to Difficult. Quantitative section was the toughest, with many advanced calculations and a tight 15‑minute limit. General Awareness was Moderate with many 2023 current‑affairs items. English was mostly Easy to Moderate with spelling and synonym questions being easy.

intro: On 27 October 2026 the SSC CGL Tier 1 exam was held in three shifts. Shift 1 has been reported as overall Easy to Moderate, with Reasoning generally Moderate, Quantitative the toughest section, General Awareness moderate and English mostly Easy to Moderate. The reported range of 20–78 good attempts for this shift is unofficial and SSC normalises scores across all shifts. Shifts 2 and 3 are still pending; no usable analysis is published yet and additional candidate evidence is required.

faqs.a: Shift 1, which has been reported, was described as Easy to Moderate overall. The other two shifts are still pending and no overall difficulty assessment is available for them yet.

faqs.q: How did the Quantitative section perform on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: In the reported shift (Shift 1) the Quantitative section was identified as the toughest part, featuring advanced calculations and a tight 15‑minute limit. No data is available for the pending shifts.

faqs.q: Are the goodAttempts numbers for 27 October 2026 reliable?

faqs.q: Why is there no analysis for shifts 2 and 3 on 27 October 2026?
faqs.a: Both Shift 2 and Shift 3 are marked as pending because sufficient candidate evidence has not yet been collected. No usable analysis can be published until more data is available.

faqs.q: How does SSC handle score normalization across shifts for the 27 October 2026 exam?
faqs.a: SSC applies a normalisation process that adjusts scores from each shift to a common scale, ensuring fairness when comparing candidates across different shift conditions.
